newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, Buba lifts marks late.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, Buba lifts marks late.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, with marks finding renewed support after a Bundesbank official said financial markets need not have an "explosive reaction" to a late European Monetary Union, analysts said.
Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen made the comments in New York at a luncheon sponsored by the American Council on Germany.
They said his comments sparked interbank demand for cash marks against most currencies, including the dollar.
Jochimsen's comments stymied dollar buying after a U.S. Treasury aide reiterated U.S. support for a strong dollar.
Senior Treasury official Jeffrey Schafer told reporters that the U.S. exchange rate policy has not changed.
Both traders and analysts were concerned the U.S. administration had remained silent after Japanese rhetoric last week suggested the dollar/yen rally may be over.
December yen fell to $0.008985, or which roughly translates into the dollar/yen's high of 111.85 spot yen, on the comments. Yen's decline dragged December marks lower.
One firm sold 200 December marks at the $0.6663 level, while one fund sold between 500 and 1,000 December yen contracts.
However, some analysts were slightly skeptical that a Treasury aide delivered the strong U.S. dollar comment, rather than U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
In addition, Jochimsen's comments soon hit the wires, and diminished any chance that the dollar would rally through 1.5100 spot, analysts said.
December marks held support at $0.6643, roughly equivalent to the dollar/mark's daily high of 1.5090 spot.
Despite the late flurry of comments, December marks still traded inside Tuesday's pit trade range of $0.6696 and $0.6637, or 1.4890 spot -- a 2-1/2-month low -- and 1.5096.

Cash marks, however, advanced against most currencies, with the mark/Swiss franc cross rate rising above a key technical level. Lower overnight Swiss rates undermined Swiss franc futures throughout the day, one analyst said.

The forex market had little reaction to the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged. The 0.3-percent decline in the core Producer Price Index (PPI) solidified expectations that the FOMC would not tighten monetary policy, they said.
U.S. October Consumer Price Index will be released at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
CPI is seen rising 0.3 percent overall against up 0.3 percent in September, and the core rate is expected to rise 0.2 percent, versus September's gain of 0.3 percent.
After pit futures closed, Jochimsen said that the dollar is more likely to appreciate against the mark than to fall.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was off $0.000015 at $0.008991, marks were up $0.0011 at $0.6654, Swiss francs were steady at $0.7909, sterling was $0.0142 higher at a contract high settlement of $1.6590, Canadian dollars were $0.0007 lower at $0.7514, Australian dollars were $0.0001 lower at $0.7871 and Mexican pesos were $0.000125 lower at $0.123200. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
